newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Equity Office tops NYSE at debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Equity Office tops NYSE at debut.

text.p: Equity Office Properties Inc jumped after the initial public offering of the real estate investment trust headed by Samuel Zell, making it the busiest stock on the New York Exchange.
Shares rose 4-1/2 to 25-1/2 after the market debut of the company, which sold 25 million shares for $21 each. The shares priced at the high end of an estimated range of $19 to $21.
Because of high demand, the number of shares to be sold was raised by 10 million by lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co.

The stock is a hot commodity because of the star-like status of its chairman, Samuel Zell, analysts said, and its relatively low debt load. The real estate mogul has made a fortune buying depressed properties and turning them around.

Zell also owns Manufactured Home Communities Inc, which owns 69 mobile home communities, and Equity Residential Properties Trust. With such buying clout, analysts say the perception is he can get low prices for properties.

Equity Office said it controls the largest office portfolio of any U.S. publicly traded companies with 32.2 million rentable square feet and 1996 revenues of about $508 million in revenues, according to its prospectus materials. It owns 90 office properties and 14 parking facilities.
It said proceeds from the offering are to be used to pay down debt, which totalled about $1.6 billion as of March 31.
-- Axiom Inc shares were up 5/8 to 12-5/8 at midday after their IPO debut. The Moorestown, N.J., company's software is used to collect billing data.
Axiom sold 2.6 million shares for $12 each, the middle of price talk of $11 to $13.

The software collects data from wireline telecommunications switches and transmits it to Axiom customers, telecommunications companies, which can then bill their own subscribers. It is also developing systems to process data from wireless, and asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) and other specialized telecommunications switches.
Axiom's largest customers include regional bell operating companies (RBOCs) such as Ameritech Corp, and international providers such as Telecom Argentina.

-- Allstar Systems Inc rose 5/16 to 6-5/16, after the company sharply cut back terms of its IPO in its second try at going public. It sold 1,767,500 shares for $6 each in the offering from Sutro & Co, well below an initial filing of 2,035,000 shares to sell at $8-$10.
In November, the company scotched a proposal to go public through underwriter Rauscher Pierce Refnes. The Houston company provides computer and telecommunications hardware and software products.

-- World of Science Inc WOSI.O shares were flat at $6 after it cut the price for shares to $6 from price talk of $8 to $9. Less shares were sold, 2.45 million, from an original plan to sell 2.6 million. Of the total number of shares, 1.6 million were sold by the company and 850,000 were sold by selling shareholders.
